summary: On the rooftop, with the roof-access tower "now engulfed in flames," Neo and Trinity stand over "a pile of their fallen enemies" as the PILOT in an army helicopter reports "we are under attack!" The pilot then dissolves, "consumed by spreading locust-like swarm of static as Agent Jones emerges." Trinity and Neo both realize the danger, and Neo whirls around firing both guns, but the magazines empty without stopping Jones, who "charges." Neo calls for "Trinity! ... Help." As Jones closes in, Neo enters bullet-time, twisting and bending between the bullets but still getting winged: a round "shears open his shoulder" and another "digs a red groove across his thigh," leaving him on the ground as Jones stands over him, raises his gun, and says "Only human..." A "sharp metal click" makes Jones whirl around into "the muzzle of Trinity's .45 -- jammed tight to his head." Trinity says "Dodge this!" and fires, blowing Jones back in "a flash of mercurial light," and when the body lands "it is the pilot." Trinity helps Neo up and asks, "how did you do that?" She marvels, "You moved like they moved. I've never seen anyone move that fast," but Neo replies, "It wasn't fast enough." After checking his shoulder and confirming he is fine, Neo insists "we have to keep moving," then sees the helicopter and asks, "Can you fly that thing?" Trinity answers, "Not yet," and "pulls out the cellular phone."

what_changes.before: In control, having taken over the pilot's body and charging at Neo with the upper hand.
what_changes.after: Destroyed — shot at point-blank range by Trinity and reduced back to the fallen pilot's body.
what_changes.evidence: jammed tight to his head ... BOOM!  BOOM!  BOOM!  The body flies back with a flash of mercurial light and when it hits the ground, it is the pilot.

what_changes.before: Unaware he can move like an Agent; he only knows the threat behind him.
what_changes.after: Has moved with superhuman speed for the first time, though he judges it insufficient.
what_changes.evidence: You moved like they moved.  I've never seen anyone move that fast. ... It wasn't fast enough.

what_changes.before: Fighting at full strength atop the pile of enemies.
what_changes.after: Wounded — shoulder sheared open and thigh grooved — but able to keep going.
what_changes.evidence: a spiraling gray ball shears open his shoulder.  ... another digs a red groove across his thigh. ... I'm fine.  Come on, we have to keep moving.

what_changes.before: About to be overwhelmed, with Neo down and Jones raising his gun for the kill.
what_changes.after: Saved by Trinity's intervention; the pair regroup and prepare to escape via the helicopter.
what_changes.evidence: Immediately, he whirls around and turns straight into the muzzle of Trinity's .45 ... Trinity helps Neo up.

event_hint.one_line: Agent Jones ambushes Neo and Trinity on the roof; after a bullet-time gunfight, Trinity kills Jones and the two prepare to flee in the helicopter.

uncertain: Whether the 'pilot' whose body remains is dead or merely vacated by the Agent.
Whether Neo's new speed is a permanent change or a one-time occurrence.

minds.wants: To survive the Agent's charge and, failing to stop it with guns, to buy the split second Trinity needs to end it.
minds.feels: A vertiginous shock under the adrenaline: for the first time the world slowed to his command, and he moved inside that space the way the Agents do. The fact that it worked is more terrifying and more significant than the fact that it nearly wasn't enough — he has just touched a capacity he doesn't understand and can't yet trust.
minds.shows: Reflex and grit — he whirls and fires, and when it fails he can only call out "Trinity! ... Help," a raw admission of dependence. Afterward he downplays everything: deflects ("Do what?"), judges his own miracle harshly ("It wasn't fast enough"), and pivots hard to the practical ("I'm fine. Come on, we have to keep moving").
minds.basis: His bullet-time is described as entering 'the liquid space' where he 'twists, bends, ducks just between them' — an involuntary-seeming mastery. His 'Do what?' is genuine incomprehension, and 'It wasn't fast enough' reframes a near-impossible feat as a shortfall. 'I'm fine' contradicts the visible shoulder and thigh wounds. He then immediately redirects to the helicopter and escape.

believes_about.belief: That he failed — he was too slow and got hurt, and only Trinity's arrival saved him.
believes_about.wrong_because: He has actually done something no human, and arguably no one he's seen, can do — move like an Agent. He measures himself against an ideal he doesn't yet know he's supposed to reach, so he reads a first, staggering success as a failure.

believes_about.belief: That a magazine emptied into a charging Agent can stop him — the ordinary rules of a firefight still apply.
believes_about.wrong_because: An Agent cannot be killed by bullets; the rounds pass through or are irrelevant until Trinity fires the kill shot that reverts Jones to the pilot. His gunfire was only ever delay, not damage.

minds.wants: To get to Neo and kill the Agent before it kills him — and, once they're breathing, to understand what she just witnessed him do.
minds.feels: Two beats in rapid succession: pure tactical terror when she sees 'the fear in her face' reflected in Neo and knows what's behind him, then a focused, almost cold precision as she closes in and executes the save. Under the relief is a dawning awe — she has spent her life knowing exactly how Agents move, and Neo just moved like one.
minds.shows: She says almost nothing during the violence; her intervention is physical and total — the .45 'jammed tight to his head,' then 'Dodge this!' and the shots. Afterward she lets her wonder show openly: 'how did you do that?', 'You moved like they moved. I've never seen anyone move that fast.' She masks her fear for him as a practical question ('Are you all right?') and immediately moves to the exit plan by pulling out the phone.
minds.basis: She 'sees what's coming' and reacts while Neo is still turning. Her kill is described with decisive, intimate force. Her post-fight dialogue is the only place she names what happened, and her phrasing ('like they moved') frames Neo against the Agents specifically, not against ordinary humans. She answers his 'Are you all right?' by refocusing on escape ('Not yet' + phone).

believes_about.belief: That he has crossed some threshold into the kind of ability the prophecy promised — that he is becoming what Morpheus insisted he could be.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is not wrong; if anything she is now more convinced than before. But she may believe he did it deliberately or understands it, when his 'Do what?' shows he acted without knowing how — the gap between her faith in his mastery and his own confusion is where their dynamic will strain.

believes_about.belief: That firing into him at point-blank range ends the threat the way it would end a man.
believes_about.wrong_because: She has done this before and knows Agents revert to a host body, but the scene's residue — the body that 'is the pilot' — means a human may now be dead because of the possession, a consequence she has to carry and hasn't yet registered.

minds.wants: To complete the order from sc-162 — 'Find them and destroy them' — by killing Neo while he is down.
minds.feels: Cold, unhurried certainty. He has closed the distance against a full magazine, stood over a wounded man, and raised his gun for the execution; 'Only human...' is genuine contempt, the satisfaction of a predator who believes the hierarchy of the world has just been confirmed.
minds.shows: A calm, verbalized verdict ('Only human...') and the physical act of raising the gun — he lets Neo see the end coming. He shows no alarm until the 'sharp metal click' forces him to whirl, and by then the muzzle is already against his head; his reaction comes a beat too late.
minds.basis: His dialogue and staging — standing over Neo, raising the gun, the dismissive line — all express assured dominance. The 'sharp metal click' is what breaks his composure, and even then he is already beaten. His emergence from the pilot follows Smith's command in sc-162.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is 'only human' — a bounded, killable target beneath an Agent's notice.
believes_about.wrong_because: Seconds earlier Neo moved in bullet-time 'like they moved,' and Trinity's awe confirms it. Jones's contempt is precisely calibrated to a truth that has already changed; he is the last to know that the thing he's dismissing is the thing prophesied to end his kind.

minds.wants: Nothing legible — he is not present as himself; his body is a vehicle being used and then vacated.
minds.feels: Nothing readable: the scene shows only the Pilot's face and body dissolving into 'a locust-like swarm of static' as Jones emerges, and at the end the body reverts to 'the pilot' with no sign of consciousness, will, or reaction.
minds.shows: Nothing of his own — only the physical transformation into and out of the Agent. There is no dialogue, gesture, or decision attributable to him.
minds.basis: The text gives the Pilot no interior markers: he is consumed by static, reemerges as Jones, and reverts to an inert body on the ground. The established uncertainty ('dead or merely vacated') cannot be resolved from anything he does or shows here.

connects_back: sc-162: Agent Smith's order 'Find them and destroy them!' and Jones touching his earpiece directly motivates Jones's emergence and charge in this scene.

sc-160/161: The cable-snap ascent through the elevator shaft and the lobby explosion are what put Neo and Trinity on the roof, wounded and low on ammunition, cornered with the helicopter as their only exit.
ev-028: The rescue of Morpheus and the crashed helicopter set the entire rooftop situation; this scene is the pursuit catching up to them after that escape.
sets_up: ev-029: The regroup and the Agents discovering the roof empty — Neo and Trinity's escape via the helicopter phone is the immediate next beat this scene is driving toward.
ev-030: Trinity's need to reach a phone-booth exit, where Agent Smith ambushes her at the subway — her pulling out the cellular phone here is the first step of that flight to an exit.
Neo's first bullet-time movement sets the precedent for the growing ability Morpheus and Trinity observe in later confrontations, culminating in the subway showdown (ev-031) and beyond.
The confirmed fact that Agents revert to a host body when 'killed' raises the unresolved cost — the pilot's body left on the roof — that the story will have to reckon with.
dramatic_function: This is the first visible crack in the world's rules: it proves Neo can move like an Agent while keeping him stubbornly unaware of what that means, so the audience sees the prophecy arriving before the hero does. It also converts the Agents from unstoppable hunters into a threat that can be killed — but only by someone who knows the trick (Trinity) — which both raises the stakes of the chase and protects the mystery of Neo's identity for the confrontations to come.
